verdict_scope: Source fidelity only: all material summary claims were checked against the complete supplied classic 1996 English base rules and every distinct base Action Card in PDF pages 1–12. PASS means no material unsupported summary rule or missing source-supplied core procedure was found; it does not certify a complete playable ruling for every source-ambiguous state.
complete_core_verdict_scope: Complete-core certification withheld because consequential base-game source rulings remain unresolved. Accurate disclosure of these source gaps does not constitute complete-core PASS.

findings.source_fidelity_effect: NONE — the summary discloses the limitation rather than asserting an unsupported resolution.
findings.title: Forced Movement has no source procedure for choosing Castillo.
findings.detail: The universal movement permission allows any/all moved Caballeros into Castillo, but this action requires destination selection on disks that omit Castillo. The card provides no Castillo signal or explicit exception to that permission. The summary correctly retains the printed disk process and reports the unresolved conflict.
findings.gameplay_impact: A fellow player’s destination and resulting majorities cannot be determined in every otherwise permitted forced-movement choice.

findings.title: All-4 scoring at Castillo with mobile 4/0/0 is not expressly reconciled.
findings.detail: All-4 says score all regions with first value four and uses mobile values; a mobile 4/0/0 can be placed at Castillo. Unlike all-5, the all-4 explanation contains no explicit Castillo inclusion/exclusion. The manual gives no worked treatment of this combination. The summary does not decide whether this triggers hidden-Castillo scoring.
findings.gameplay_impact: The scoring set, points, and visibility of Castillo contents may differ. This audit does not certify either proposed interpretation as an authoritative ruling.

findings.title: Mandatory returns can demand more eligible pieces than a player has.
findings.detail: The King returns demands three own pieces from court and unprotected board regions, but has no shortfall rule. Send-one-from-each demands a board piece for every color but has no zero-eligible fallback. Adjacent Decay cards explicitly supply their own shortfall rules; those are not stated as universal. The summary correctly identifies both omissions.
findings.gameplay_impact: The required return and completion of the special action are unspecified for reachable zero/shortfall states.

findings.title: Secret return cards do not fully reconcile participation and protected-only states.
findings.detail: Both headings/card faces assign removal to fellow players; explanatory paragraphs instead say all players must select a disk. It is not clear whether the selector must make an otherwise purposeless legal selection or participate further. The two-return fallback assumes some one-piece region; the all-return exception covers no pieces in any region but does not cover pieces confined to the King region. Neither provides a legal selection procedure when all possible qualifying regions are protected. The summary exposes these distinctions.
findings.gameplay_impact: A player can be unable to satisfy the mandatory disk selection/count requirement while the taboo prohibits the only candidate; participation and action completion need a ruling.

conflict_resolution_review.result: Supported source-priority reading, transparently disclosed. The detailed paragraph and matching embedded card face both say each player. conflict_resolution_review.result: Faithful preservation rather than unsupported universal restriction. This audit does not add a ruling beyond the actual wording.

source_limitations: Only the assigned snapshot, complete extracted/el-grande-rules.txt, and direct text of authoritative source_pdfs/el-grande-publisher-rules.pdf pages 1–12 were inspected. No questions, keys, readers, grades, prior reviews, source-gap register, fan translation, later edition, expansion pages 13–20, external source or browsing was used.

All twelve PDF pages were read directly using pypdf, including embedded printed-card text, and compared with the supplied extraction; no graphic rendering was available. This is a textual rules audit, not a physical-component or illustrated-board geometry inspection.
The source provides no further endgame tiebreaker. The summary reports this absence accurately; this audit does not create one.
The optional six-round game is expressly outside the assigned scope.
The snapshot carries an existing inaccurate/pending-review banner. Its audit-history assertions were not independently investigated and do not establish a new rules discrepancy.
